fatal_errors: It replaces the target AlCoCrFeNi atmospheric-plasma-sprayed coating and 550 °C anneal with severe-plastic-deformation grain refinement of an unspecified stainless steel.
The cited evidence does not establish grain-boundary-accelerated chromium diffusion or self-healing as the governing cause.

Severe plastic deformation changes residual stress, defect density, texture, and phase stability in addition to grain size, so the proposed comparison cannot uniquely attribute corrosion behavior to grain-boundary chromium transport.
The proposed aqueous chloride exposure near 300 °C omits the target sulfuric-acid electrochemistry and 900 °C Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion regimes.
explanation: The hypothesis is testable and scientifically plausible as a general alternative: chromium-rich passive films commonly protect stainless steels, and a coarse-grained control, electrochemical measurements, XPS, and pit imaging could detect a grain-size-associated improvement. It also predicts lower corrosion currents and less pitting, directionally overlapping the target. However, it does not reconstruct the paper's material system, APS coating, annealing series, phase structure, hardness response, or molten-salt tests. Mechanistic agreement is limited to chromium passivation and a broad grain-refinement benefit; the target instead emphasizes an AlCoCrFeNi coating, Al- and Cr-rich oxides, high-entropy/sluggish-diffusion behavior, and delayed salt penetration through coating defects. E1 supports the protective role of Cr2O3 but not the asserted grain-boundary transport mechanism. E2 discusses molten fluoride salts and notes that chromium can be preferentially attacked, so it does not support the claimed aqueous UFG mechanism and limits its generalization to nuclear environments. A stronger causal test would independently vary grain size while controlling residual stress and texture, directly measure chromium transport or film-repassivation kinetics, and compare interrupted film-damage recovery rates. The source target was also retracted, a limitation absent from the generated answer.
